subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core `plugins install/uninstall --agent` contract now, and what install-record identity, update, discovery, runtime activation, and security semantics should that contract use?
rationale: The PR changes public CLI behavior, persisted plugin install identity, workspace code-execution roots, and multi-agent isolation semantics; automation cannot choose that permanent product/security contract from the patch alone.

options.title: Pause behind the canonical design issue
options.body: Keep this PR open or ask for a redesign until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97749 has a maintainer-approved contract covering install, uninstall, update, discovery, trust, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Proceed with a complete scoped lifecycle PR
options.body: Authorize this direction only if the contributor fixes the current lifecycle blockers and adds proof for install, uninstall, update, unknown-agent rejection, and shared-config preservation.

options.title: Reject core-scoped installs for now
options.body: Close or redirect the implementation if maintainers decide per-agent plugin isolation should be solved through another plugin/API or configuration mechanism instead.

recommendation.title: Pause behind the canonical design issue
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open or ask for a redesign until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97749 has a maintainer-approved contract covering install, uninstall, update, discovery, trust, and upgrade behavior.
